correctness.rationale: With one work register and a passive output, basic work-register updates are constants. Two nonzero work-register accesses must cancel, so every nonlinear two-call program reduces to H(tau+a x)-H(tau), forcing H-H(0) and hence f-f(0) to be additive. The converse two-call transcript is exact. Classical additive-polynomial classification then gives the characteristic-p unbounded-degree family.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper proves the two-call and two-register degree frontiers only in characteristic zero and does not discuss Frobenius or additive polynomials. The 2025 register-program paper gives four-access positive-characteristic constructions but no matching two-call classification. Targeted external and SCOPE searches found no equivalent statement. The claim remains narrow and carries material folklore and near-simultaneous priority risk.

value.rationale: The result shows the characteristic-zero assumption is maximally essential: in positive characteristic, two accesses and one work register already support arbitrarily high formal degree. It also gives an exact iff description of the two-register two-call class and identifies additive finite differences as the mechanism.
